ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is folded along line MN such that point A coincides with point E on side AB. If $\angle B=54^\circ$ and $\angle C=90^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle ENC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} 
\[
\because \angle B=54^\circ, \angle C=90^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle A=90^\circ-\angle B=36^\circ,
\]
From the property of folding, we get:
\[
\angle AEN=\angle A=36^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle ENC=\angle AEN+\angle A=\boxed{72^\circ}.
\]

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is folded along line MN such that point A coincides with point E on side AB. If $\angle B=54^\circ$ and $\angle C=90^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle ENC$?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} \[ \because \angle B=54^\circ,\ \angle C=90^\circ, \] \[ \therefore \angle A=90^\circ-\angle B=36^\circ, \] From the property of folding, we get: \[ \angle AEN=\angle A=36^\circ, \] \[ \therefore \angle ENC=\angle AEN+\angle A=\boxed{72^\circ}. \]
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is right triangle ABC, a right angle is marked at C, AC is the horizontal base, BC is vertical upward, and B is at the upper right. E is located on side AB, N is located on side AC, and the crease is MN; the dashed lines show the original A connected to M and N, after folding A coincides with E on AB, and the gray region indicates the folded part. Then reason: Given ∠B=54°, ∠C=90°, so ∠A=180°−54°−90°=36°. The folding is a reflection about MN, and MN is the perpendicular bisector of AE, therefore N is on the crease and satisfies NA=NE, so triangle AEN is an isosceles triangle. Also because E is on AB and N is on AC, ∠EAN is exactly ∠A of the original triangle, namely 36°, so ∠AEN=36°. In the figure NC is the extension of NA, so ∠ENC is the exterior angle of triangle AEN at point N, equal to ∠EAN+∠AEN=36°+36°=72°.
